# T08 Plan: queryDsl escaping/precedence/nulls + BatchIngestor serialization/rollback

## Context
Both visible tests in `test/task_visible.test.mjs` fail at baseline (`node --test`):
- `path == "C:\\temp\\"` throws "Unterminated string literal": the scanner treats `"` as escaped whenever the previous char is `\`, so it can't tell `\\"` (escaped backslash followed by the closing quote) from `\"`. It also never unescapes anything.
- `a == 1 OR b == 2 AND c == 3`: `parseExpr` folds AND and OR left to right at the same level, so it parses as `(a OR b) AND c`.
- The sink-rejection test: `flush()` splices the buffer before `await sinkFn`, so a rejection loses the batch (pendingCount 0 instead of 2).
- There's also no mutex, so concurrent `ingest()`/`flush()` calls can run `sinkFn` at the same time.

Only two files change: `src/queryDsl.mjs` and `src/batchIngestor.mjs`. `src/errors.mjs` already has `ERR_DSL_SYNTAX` and `LedgerError`. No `eval`/`new Function` (the current code uses neither). `frozenWire.mjs` and `errors.mjs` are not touched.

## 1. `src/queryDsl.mjs`

### `tokenizeDsl` string branch (replace the lines handling `ch === '"'`)
- Scan from `j = i + 1` with an explicit escape state machine:
  - On `\`: if `j + 1 >= expr.length`, throw `LedgerError(ERR_DSL_SYNTAX, 'Dangling escape')`. Otherwise map the next char: `\\`→`\`, `"`→`"`, `n`→`\n`, `t`→`\t`. Any other char throws `ERR_DSL_SYNTAX` ('Invalid escape sequence'). Then `j += 2`.
  - On unescaped `"`: the string is closed. Push `{type:'STRING', value: buf}` and set `i = j + 1`.
  - Otherwise append the char and `j += 1`.
- If the loop runs out of input before a closing quote, throw `ERR_DSL_SYNTAX` ('Unterminated string literal').
- Result: `"C:\\temp\\"` gives `C:\temp\`. Inputs like `"abc`, `"abc\"` and `"abc\` all throw.

### `resolveField`
- Keep returning `undefined` when the current value is null or not an object. Also return `undefined` when `part` isn't an own property (`Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(cur, part)`), so a missing path never resolves to a prototype member like `toString` or `constructor`.

### Comparison semantics (extract a helper `compareValues(op, actual, target)`)
- `isNullish = v => v === null || v === undefined`
- `isBad = v => isNullish(v) || (typeof v === 'number' && Number.isNaN(v))`
- `==`: return true if both sides are nullish, otherwise `actual === target`.
- `!=`: the negation of `==`. So `missing != "x"` is true and `missing != null` is false.
- `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`: return false if either side `isBad`, otherwise use the native comparison.

### Parser: strict precedence `()` > `NOT` > `AND` > `OR`
Replace `parseExpr` and the NOT branch inside `parsePrimary` with this chain:
- `parseOr()`: `left = parseAnd()`, then loop while the next token is `OR`.
- `parseAnd()`: `left = parseNot()`, then loop while the next token is `AND`.
